searchText: As I remember: * Average witness size (assuming binary trees and code merklization): ~500-700 kB * Theoretical max witness size (assuming targeted "attack blocks" and my proposed gas repricings): ~3-4 MB We have had 500 kB blocks on mainnet before as part of starkware's tests, and it did disrupt some bootstrap nodes as I remember, though mining was completely un-disrupted; no noticeable change in uncle rate Technically, clients would not need to *store* witnesses As witnesses can be recomputed > Would it lead to lower gas limits to compensate? I actually hope that stateless can open the door to *higher* gas limits! Another thing to keep in mind is that in the longer run (2+ years?) the witness size drops to ~100-200 kB because we'll have witness compression with fancy SNARK/STARKs > Technically, clients would not need to store witnesses > As witnesses can be recomputed > I actually hope that stateless can open the door to higher gas limits! Right, since state size will be lower, but I would imagine it would take much longer to sync a full node if we raise the gas limit, especially if dealing with witnessess slows down validation (which I assume it does, but may not). > he witness size drops to ~100-200 kB because we'll have witness compression with fancy SNARK/STARKs Yeah using these would def make witnesses a lot more interesting, though this does seem indeed like a 3-5 years vision and imo might be dangeroud to rely on for short/medium term decisions. > especially if dealing with witnessess slows down validation (which I assume it does, but may not). It may actually speed it up no more disk accesses needed Readily available witnesses from the network potentially do away with the *need* for an SSD as you can do all of your reads from the witness, and only use the disk for batched writes. (Implicitely this also should speed up block processing/validation) Interesting, that makes sense! Glad to hear that, thanks for clearing this up for me 😄

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
As I remember:

* Average witness size (assuming binary trees and code merklization): ~500-700 kB
* Theoretical max witness size (assuming targeted "attack blocks" and my proposed gas repricings): ~3-4 MB

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: We have had 500 kB blocks on mainnet before as part of starkware's tests, and it did disrupt some bootstrap nodes as I remember, though mining was completely un-disrupted; no noticeable change in uncle rate

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Technically, clients would not need to *store* witnesses

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content:
> Would it lead to lower gas limits to compensate?

I actually hope that stateless can open the door to *higher* gas limits!

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: Another thing to keep in mind is that in the longer run (2+ years?) the witness size drops to ~100-200 kB because we'll have witness compression with fancy SNARK/STARKs

excerpts.author: phabc
excerpts.content:
> Technically, clients would not need to store witnesses
> As witnesses can be recomputed
> I actually hope that stateless can open the door to higher gas limits!
Right, since state size will be lower, but I would imagine it would take much longer to sync a full node if we raise the gas limit, especially if dealing with witnessess slows down validation (which I assume it does, but may not).

> he witness size drops to ~100-200 kB because we'll have witness compression with fancy SNARK/STARKs
Yeah using these would def make witnesses a lot more interesting, though this does seem indeed like a 3-5 years vision and imo might be dangeroud to rely on for short/medium term decisions.

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: > especially if dealing with witnessess slows down validation (which I assume it does, but may not).

excerpts.author: .vbuterin
excerpts.content: It may actually speed it up

excerpts.author: pipermerriam
excerpts.content: Readily available witnesses from the network potentially do away with the *need* for an SSD as you can do all of your reads from the witness, and only use the disk for batched writes.  (Implicitely this also should speed up block processing/validation)

excerpts.content: Interesting, that makes sense! Glad to hear that, thanks for clearing this up for me 😄
